items.comparator: Researchers’ estimated manual effort to build the knowledge base; no separate benchmark or controlled comparison is described.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Without using this technology, it would have taken our researchers a year to create the knowledge base. Using AI, it took us a couple of hours.” The team gathered 62,000 patents and 44,000 abstracts; it then developed several hypotheses for testing in about six weeks.
items.signal: Saint-Gobain researchers used Microsoft Discovery to assemble and analyze a large patent-and-abstract knowledge base for cement additives. The claimed time reduction is a workflow benefit; the article does not establish that the result is difficult for competitors to reproduce.
items.source: Microsoft, reporting remarks by Saint-Gobain digital acceleration program manager Mojdeh Rastgoo-Lemaitre

items.comparator: The article reports a before-and-after selectivity figure, but does not specify a controlled baseline or comparison method.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article says Mira “pushed a single-step reaction's selectivity from 51.82% to 85% in three months.” It also reports a specialty-chemicals project where the company says it improved production yield “from 72% to nearly 90%.”
items.signal: The company describes an AI-guided autonomous laboratory loop that designs, runs and evaluates experiments. The reported chemical results are candidate operating benefits, but are company-reported and the article does not supply independent validation or enough detail to assess reproducibility.
items.source: ACCESS Newswire article about Deep Principle; carried by Yahoo Finance

items.comparator: For polymer workflow, the source compares automated operation with a typical 8-hour operation window and a maximum of three samples prepared sequentially. For alloy screening, it states a comparison with conventional methods but does not give further benchmark details.
items.quantitative_outcome: The release says the polymer workflow changed from a typical 8-hour operation window and a maximum of three sequentially prepared samples to 24-hour continuous operation with up to 25 prepared in parallel, producing 75 samples in 24 hours—“around 25 times the daily output.” It also says alloy methods can screen up to 470 unique samples a day, “more than 400 times” conventional throughput.
items.signal: MARVEL-AI describes automation and AI-enabled materials workflows with substantial stated throughput gains. The figures suggest capability and operating benefit, but are initiative-reported and do not by themselves establish a durable competitive advantage for a particular company.
items.vertical: Advanced materials, including polymers, alloys, semiconductors, energy and chemicals

items.company: TOPPAN Holdings, AISIN, Asahi Kasei, SoftBank, AGC and DIC
items.signal: The six companies announced joint research combining quantum computing and AI for materials development, including battery, optical, superconducting and semiconductor-related materials. The project is planned for fiscal 2026–2028 and is still testing practicality; no measured benefit or distinctive proprietary-data outcome is reported.
items.source: LC Signal, reporting the companies’ announcement
items.vertical: Battery, optical, superconducting and semiconductor materials

items.quantitative_outcome: The announced Cascade dataset is planned to combine 100 million single-cell RNA-seq profiles with more than 11,000 proteomic secretome profiles across more than 150,000 perturbation conditions. This is a data-access move, not a reported operating outcome; none stated.
items.signal: The companies announced a partnership to build a large multimodal immune-biology dataset, with foundational commitments from GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, Graph Therapeutics, and Turbine. If access or coverage proves distinctive, it could support AI-enabled target discovery that is difficult for competitors to replicate.
items.source: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio press release carried by Business Wire

items.signal: Apheris said its federated research networks for drug discovery and European healthcare studies can run on T-Systems’ sovereign infrastructure, with patient data remaining inside each hospital. This is a distinctive access/infrastructure arrangement, not a measured operating benefit.

items.comparator: Trade-document processing turnaround time before the AI-enabled workflows; no exact baseline stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “AI-enabled workflows reduced trade-document processing turnaround times by over 70%.”
items.signal: Reported a large reduction in trade-document processing time. This is a workflow-efficiency signal, but the source does not describe the baseline period or establish that the capability is difficult for competitors to reproduce.

items.comparator: AI-agent testing cycle versus the prior average development cycle for an updated version; the reported comparison is 4.4 days versus 21.2 days.
items.quantitative_outcome: “testing AI agents on simulated customers had shortened the average development cycle for an updated version from 21.2 days to 4.4 days.”
items.signal: A measured shortening of an AI-agent testing cycle. It is a workflow signal; the report does not establish a durable competitive advantage or quantify broader business impact.
items.source: The Asian Banker, summarizing Nubank’s report and Reuters coverage

items.comparator: £17.9 million identified by connected AI and advanced analytics out of £109.3 million in total detected over the past year; no non-AI comparator stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “£17.9 million of £109.3 million detected over the past year.”
items.signal: Reported a quantified contribution to detected fake claims. The source does not provide a counterfactual or show that this result is hard for competitors to copy; the distinctive potential lies in the insurer’s claims data and fraud-network information.
items.source: Insurewire, reporting Zurich UK’s claim and identifying Quantexa as the technology partner

items.comparator: Portfolio modelling previously took a week; the new reported time is 10 to 20 minutes.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Portfolio modelling that previously took a week now takes 10 to 20 minutes.”
items.signal: A substantial reported throughput improvement in capital-markets loan-tape processing and portfolio modelling. This is a measured workflow benefit; the source does not specify a controlled comparison or identify a proprietary dataset.

items.comparator: Respectively, SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym, and CWE-bench; the source also says Chrome's internal patch-generation comparison was against other frontier models, without giving a specific comparator or a number for that comparison.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report states: “88.2% on SEC-bench Pro” for vulnerability discovery, “54.8% on ExploitGym” for exploitation assessment, and “71% on CWE-bench” for patching. It also reports a 10x patch-quality improvement in internal Chrome-team evaluations versus competitor models, as summarized in the article. These are benchmark or internal-evaluation results, not measured production outcomes.
items.signal: Google’s reported cybersecurity benchmark scores and restricted access for selected defenders are a possible capability signal; they do not establish a hard-to-copy operating advantage.

items.comparator: AI security assessment agents operating with deception techniques deployed versus baseline runs without those techniques, as summarized in the source.
items.quantitative_outcome: The source summary reports: deception “raised model spend per objective 23x from $1.33 to $31.10,” “extended time-to-first-objective 7.8x,” and “cut combined objective success 91% from 2.48 to 0.23 per run.” It also reports Chinese models completed objectives in 98% of baseline runs and 0% with the techniques deployed.
items.signal: A measured defensive effect across 773 assessments may indicate an operational benefit from Tracebit’s deception techniques; the result is vendor-reported and the durability or transferability of the advantage is not established here.
items.source: Tracebit, as identified by AI Weekly’s deployment summary

items.comparator: Rolling-force prediction hit rate: 88% before, 98% after. Metallographic inspection time: 10 minutes per sample before, 3–5 minutes after. The source also reports annual costs falling by over CNY100 million, but gives no cost baseline.
items.quantitative_outcome: NISCO and Huawei’s release, as summarized in the original case-study article, reports: “The rolling-force prediction hit rate rose from 88% to 98%”; “inspection of a steel sample fell from 10 minutes to 3–5 minutes”; and “annual costs fell by over CNY100 million.” The article says these figures come from the companies’ release and have not been independently measured.
items.signal: AI models and agents deployed across steelmaking workflows, with reported gains in rolling-force prediction, laboratory inspection time, and annual costs. This is a weak competitive-advantage signal: outcomes are quantified but company-reported, without independent validation; the cost comparison baseline is unspecified.
items.source: Case Studies AI, reporting on NISCO and Huawei’s October 26 release

items.comparator: No explicit before/after comparator stated in the available result; reported as an improvement during the New York City trial. Ericsson is the technology partner.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports that T-Mobile and Ericsson’s live New York City trials delivered a “16% improvement in downlink user throughput” and “12% higher spectral efficiency.”
items.signal: AI-managed beamforming trial in a live network with quantified throughput and spectral-efficiency gains. Weak competitive-advantage signal: the outcome is a trial report, and the available source does not specify a baseline, measurement method, or independent evaluator.
items.source: TeckNexus, October 2026 AI and automation roundup

items.comparator: Compared with 49 demand-response events in 2025, the 2026 figure is 73 events, according to the reported release. No prior-year demand-reduction total is stated in the available result.
items.quantitative_outcome: Oracle states that Opower programs delivered “1 gigawatt (GW) of demand reduction” across “more than 70” winter and summer events. A roundup reports 73 events in 2026 versus 49 in 2025 and an average 16,592 kW saved per event; the original release excerpt does not state those latter figures.
items.signal: Utility customers using Oracle Opower programs reportedly reduced peak demand by 1 GW year to date. This is a weak signal: the outcome is quantified by the vendor, but it aggregates customer programs and does not identify a specific utility, comparator for the 1 GW figure, or independent measurement.
